🔎 Main Ideas from the Poster

🐧

UNIX → Linux → Ubuntu

UNIX is an older operating system family; Linux is a Unix-like open-source kernel; Ubuntu is a Linux distribution.

💻

Windows vs. Linux

Windows is generally proprietary. Linux is open source and helps us study operating system concepts.

📦

Virtual Machine

VirtualBox can run Ubuntu as a guest OS while Windows remains the host OS.

⚙️

Prepare Ubuntu

Install VirtualBox, download the Ubuntu ISO, create a VM, select the ISO, install Ubuntu, and open Terminal.

⌨️

Terminal

Type commands to communicate with the operating system and inspect its files, folders, and system information.

📁

Common Commands

Practice whoami, pwd, ls, mkdir, cd, date, and uname -a.

Lesson 1 – What Are UNIX, Linux, and Ubuntu?

Understand the operating system before using it.

📖 First: Explanation and Example

UNIX is an older family of operating systems. Linux is an open-source, Unix-like operating system kernel. Ubuntu is a Linux distribution that includes the kernel, software, tools, and a desktop environment. In this lab, we will use Ubuntu.

UNIXAn older family of operating systems.
LinuxA Unix-like, open-source operating system kernel.
UbuntuA Linux distribution used for this course.
TerminalA place to type commands and see results.
Ubuntu Terminal — example commands
# Open Terminal in Ubuntu with Ctrl + Alt + T
whoami
uname -a
Example output (your result may differ)
student
Linux ubuntu 6.x.x-... x86_64 GNU/Linux

Your username and Linux version will be different.
💡 Ubuntu is the operating system we will work with in our Linux labs.

Lesson 2 – How Can Ubuntu Run on a Windows Laptop?

Understand the host, VirtualBox, and guest system.

📖 First: Explanation and Example

Most students already use Windows. We can keep Windows as the host operating system and run Ubuntu inside a virtual machine using Oracle VirtualBox. A virtual machine uses part of the real computer’s resources.

Windows (Host OS)The main operating system on the physical laptop.
Oracle VirtualBoxSoftware that creates and manages virtual machines.
Ubuntu (Guest OS)Linux running inside the virtual machine.
Virtual MachineA software-based computer inside your real computer.
Ubuntu Terminal — example commands
# In Ubuntu Terminal, check your current user:
whoami

# Check your location in Ubuntu:
pwd
Example output (your result may differ)
student
/home/student

The name and path depend on your Ubuntu account.
💡 The poster shows an example VM with 4 GB RAM. This is an example, not a required setting for every computer.

Lesson 3 – How Can We Communicate with Linux?

Practice the basic Terminal commands.

📖 First: Explanation and Example

The Terminal lets us send text commands to Ubuntu. We can ask for our username, current directory, files and folders, the date, and information about the Linux system.

whoamiDisplay the current username.
pwdDisplay the current directory path.
lsList files and folders.
date / uname -aShow the current date / system information.
Ubuntu Terminal — example commands
whoami
pwd
ls
date
uname -a
Example output (your result may differ)
student
/home/student
Desktop  Documents  Downloads
Tue Oct 13 15:30:00 +04 2026
Linux ubuntu 6.x.x-... x86_64 GNU/Linux

The date, folders, and Linux version will vary.
💡 Do not copy the example output exactly. Your real Terminal will show your own username, date, and system details.

Lesson 4 – How Can We Navigate and Create a Folder?

Use ls, cd, and mkdir in Ubuntu.

📖 First: Explanation and Example

Linux stores files inside directories. We use ls to see what is available, cd to move between folders, and mkdir to create a new folder. These are the foundation of file and directory management.

lsList files and folders.
cd folderMove into a named folder.
cd .. / cd ~Move up one level / return to home.
mkdir nameCreate a new directory.
Ubuntu Terminal — example commands
cd ~
mkdir CSCI300
cd CSCI300
mkdir Week1Lab
ls
cd Week1Lab
pwd
cd ..
ls
Example output (your result may differ)
Week1Lab
/home/student/CSCI300/Week1Lab
Week1Lab

If CSCI300 already exists, skip mkdir CSCI300.
💡 If the CSCI300 folder already exists, do not delete it. Simply use cd CSCI300. You can also run mkdir -p CSCI300/Week1Lab to safely create both folders if needed.
